stem:
Dev asks how a numerical degree measure is assigned to an angle formed by two rays from a point.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Answer "one-degree unit", naming that phrase instead of saying how many such units lie between the arms.
Count any collection of parts of a turn as degrees, even when those parts are not equal parts of a full turn.
A full turn is split into $360$ equal one-degree parts; the angle's measure is how many of those equal parts lie between its arms.
Say that the degree reading is what creates the equal one-degree parts, instead of counting those parts between the arms.

teacher.key_rationale: Degree measure counts how many equal 1/360 turns lie between the arms. Naming the unit phrase, dropping equal-part requirement, or reversing cause miss that definition.
